metadata.case_name: South Korea and Taiwan (developmental democratic transitions)
metadata.author: V2 expansion (subagent draft)
metadata.key_test: Mod4 abstention: both near-matched developmental democracies should consolidate; the framework should ABSTAIN on ranking them against each other if the late-period P1 gap falls inside the WGI margin of error. Taiwan is NOT in the World Bank WGI dataset -> treated as DATA-LIMITED (proxy/qualitative high-capacity democracy) per the sub-state/non-WB convention; the gap is therefore unmeasurable and abstention is mandatory.
metadata.notes: Reference-based record. South Korea carries real MI v2 re-scores. Taiwan has no World Bank WGI coverage -> no resolved scores; reasoned qualitatively (mirrors how Kosovo / South Sudan / East Timor data gaps were handled). 1987-1996 transitions -> 2024; scored ~1996 vs 2024.

pre_event.event_description: Both economies completed peaceful transitions from developmental authoritarianism to electoral democracy (Korea 1987-1992; Taiwan 1987-1996 first direct presidential election), atop Confucian, Japanese-colonial, developmental-dictatorship legacies.

South Korea.notes: Inputs resolved live via mi.datasource (country_ref + year). WGI 2025-anchored 0-100. Consolidated high-capacity democracy with peaceful turnovers.

Taiwan.data_note: pre-event indicators unavailable for Taiwan at 1996 (sub-state/new-state/pre-WGI gap)

a_trajectory_ranking.prediction: Both consolidate to high-tier outcomes; ABSTAIN on ranking South Korea vs Taiwan (Mod4)
a_trajectory_ranking.basis: Near-matched developmental democracies; Taiwan is data-limited so the P1 gap is unmeasurable -> within-margin by default -> abstention mandatory
a_trajectory_ranking.falsification_condition: Either case fails to consolidate, OR a defensible same-source measurement places one decisively above the other beyond the WGI margin

b_violence.prediction: Low internal violence RISK for both (high P1, consolidated democracies)
b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY
b_violence.falsification_condition: Internal political violence or breakdown in either

c_convergence.prediction: Convergence (both rise toward the high-capacity-democracy band)
c_convergence.basis: Shared developmental-democratic trajectory; both already high P1

d_failure_dimension.prediction: No primary failure dimension expected; residual exposure is external (security environment), not institutional
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Institutional collapse on a measured pillar

f_reversal_risk.prediction: Low reversal risk for both consolidated democracies

South Korea.outcome_summary: Consolidated to the top tier: MI 0.778 -> 0.804 (Tier 2 -> Tier 1), P1 0.635 -> 0.728. Multiple peaceful turnovers; a sitting president impeached and removed by constitutional process (2017) - democratic resilience, not breakdown.

Taiwan.outcome_summary: Qualitative (no WB data): consolidated high-capacity democracy. Repeated peaceful presidential turnovers (2000, 2008, 2016, 2024), Freedom House 'Free', top-regional rule of law and control of corruption in non-WB measures. Outcome materially indistinguishable in tier from South Korea -> Mod4 abstention on ranking upheld.
key_events: high-capacity democracy sustained under cross-strait pressure

a_trajectory.evidence: Korea Tier 2 -> Tier 1; Taiwan qualitatively top-tier; intra-pair gap unmeasurable (Taiwan absent from WGI) -> Mod4 abstention honored
a_trajectory.explanation: [data-limited: an entity lacks pre-P1 or post-MI -> auto-derivation skipped, judgment preserved] [data-limited: an entity lacks pre-P1 or post-MI -> auto-derivation skipped, judgment preserved] Mod4 abstention: both consolidated as predicted, but the framework correctly declines to rank them because Taiwan is data-limited and any P1 gap is within (indeed below) the WGI margin. Coded PARTIAL to mark the abstention rather than a clean ordinal confirmation.

b_violence.evidence: No internal political violence/breakdown in either; Korea's 2017 impeachment resolved constitutionally
b_violence.data_refreshed: 2026-06-28: focus=South Korea pre-P1=0.635 -> LOW risk (MI v1, anchored)

c_convergence.evidence: Both in the high-capacity-democracy band by 2024 (Korea Tier 1; Taiwan qualitatively equivalent)
c_convergence.explanation: Convergence to the top band as predicted.

d_failure_dimension.evidence: No institutional-pillar failure in either; residual exposure is the external security environment
d_failure_dimension.explanation: No primary failure dimension materialized, as predicted.

analysis.overall_assessment: Paradigmatic peaceful authoritarian-to-democratic consolidations; both reached the top band. The Mod4 sub-test is the point of the case: with Taiwan unmeasurable in WGI, the framework abstains from an intra-pair ranking rather than manufacturing a spurious gap.
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Demonstrates Mod4 abstention discipline driven by a hard data limitation (a high-capacity polity simply absent from the source dataset), not merely by a narrow numeric gap.
analysis.baseline_impact: None; reinforces the directional/ordinal-only and Mod4 abstention rules.
analysis.data_note: Taiwan is a non-WB, data-limited entity; its scores are intentionally null and its assessment is qualitative.
analysis.phase3_note: Migrated to MI v1 + Data API references. a_trajectory/c_convergence auto-derived from real re-scored data (Mod4-gated); b/d/e/f/g/h preserved as judgment.
analysis.judgment_refresh_note: Judgment verdicts (b/d/e/f/g/h) re-examined against MI v1 real-data scores on 2026-06-28: no verdict flips (directional readings robust to the legacy->anchored vintage change); b risk-levels refreshed from real pre-P1, d augmented with the real config (weakest pillar flagged as a binding vulnerability only when below median), safeguards re-evaluated.
